questions.prompt: In WAT structured control flow, what does `br 0` inside a `block` vs a `loop` do?

options.text: Inside a `block`, `br` jumps to the end; inside a `loop`, `br` jumps back to the start of the `loop`

questions.prompt: What does `br_if $done` do in WAT?

options.text: Pops an `i32` from the stack and branches to `$done` if it is non-zero

questions.prompt: What happens to existing JavaScript `Uint8Array` views over `memory.buffer` when Wasm executes `memory.grow`?

options.text: The old `ArrayBuffer` is detached, so JS must create a new view from `memory.buffer`

questions.prompt: What does `i32.load` do with the `i32` address on top of the stack?

options.text: Stores a value at that address
Pops the byte address and pushes the 4-byte little-endian `i32` loaded from linear memory

questions.prompt: Select all statements that are true about `i32.store` in WAT. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Traps if `address + 4` exceeds current memory size
Returns the stored value on the stack
Writes 4 bytes in little-endian order into linear memory

questions.prompt: Match each WAT memory load/store instruction to its byte width.
What is a WebAssembly `(table ...)` used for?

options.text: Storing function references (`funcref`) for dynamic dispatch via `call_indirect`

questions.prompt: What does `call_indirect (type $sig)` check at runtime before invoking a table entry?

options.text: That the table index is in bounds, non-null, and matches signature `$sig` (otherwise it traps)

questions.prompt: What does `(if (result i32) (then ...) (else ...))` require in WAT?

options.text: Both `then` and `else` branches must leave an `i32` on the stack

questions.prompt: Select all valid reasons to use `WebAssembly.compileStreaming` / `instantiateStreaming` over `WebAssembly.instantiate(arrayBuffer)`. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Avoids buffering an extra full `ArrayBuffer` copy before starting compilation
Requires `application/wasm` MIME type from the server
Works without HTTP/fetch on local `file://` URLs in all browsers
Compilation begins while bytes are still downloading

questions.prompt: Why does `drop` exist as a WAT instruction?

options.text: Discards the top value from the operand stack when a call's return value isn't needed

questions.prompt: What does `select` do in WAT?

options.text: Pops `[val1, val2, cond]` and pushes `val1` if `cond != 0`, else `val2` (branchless ternary)

questions.prompt: Match each WAT control-flow construct to its behavior.

columns.label: Target for forward `br` jumps to exit the block
Target for backward `br` jumps to repeat the loop

questions.prompt: When passing a `Float64Array` of 10,000 numbers from JS to Wasm, what is the fastest pattern?

options.text: Call a Wasm function 10,000 times in a JS `for` loop
Pass each number as a separate `export`
Copy/write the array once into Wasm linear memory and run one Wasm call to process all 10,000 items

questions.prompt: What does `(start $init)` in a Wasm module do?

options.text: Runs `$init` automatically as soon as the module is instantiated

questions.prompt: How can JavaScript read a UTF-8 string written by Wasm at `(ptr, len)` in `memory.buffer`?

code.source:
const bytes = new Uint8Array(memory.buffer, ptr, len);
const text = new TextDecoder().decode(bytes);

questions.prompt: Select all statements that are true about `i32` / `i64` arithmetic in WebAssembly. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Integer addition and multiplication wrap around on overflow (two's complement)
Signed division `i32.div_s` traps on division by zero
Integer addition throws a JS exception on overflow

questions.prompt: What does `memory.size` return?

options.text: Current number of 64 KiB memory pages

questions.prompt: What does `memory.grow` return if it succeeds vs if it fails (exceeds `maximum` or host limit)?

options.text: Returns the previous page count on success, or `-1` on failure

questions.prompt: In Rust + `wasm-bindgen`, what does `#[wasm_bindgen]` on a `pub fn` do?

options.text: Generates the JS/TS glue code to convert strings, structs, and slices across the Wasm boundary

questions.prompt: Why should `wasm-opt -Oz` (or `-O3`) be run on release `.wasm` binaries?

options.text: To shrink binary size and optimize Wasm instruction sequences for faster download and execution

questions.prompt: Match each Wasm memory/data concept to its role.

columns.label: Static byte offset and alignment hint for memory access
Initializes linear memory bytes at module load
Sets initial 1 page and maximum 16 pages (1 MiB)

questions.prompt: What happens if a Wasm module is compiled with `-g` (DWARF debug info) and shipped directly to production?

options.text: The `.wasm` file becomes much larger because DWARF sections are embedded; strip or split debug info for production

questions.prompt: How does `WebAssembly.Memory({ initial: 1, maximum: 10, shared: true })` differ from normal memory?

options.text: It is backed by a `SharedArrayBuffer` so multiple Web Workers can share memory concurrently

questions.prompt: Which HTTP response headers are required by browsers to enable `SharedArrayBuffer` for Wasm threads?
What does `memory.copy` (bulk memory proposal) allow inside Wasm?

options.text: Fast, single-instruction copying of byte ranges within linear memory (like `memcpy`)

questions.prompt: Select all valid ways to debug a WebAssembly module. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Using browser DevTools with DWARF or source maps
Calling imported host `console.log` functions for trace logging

questions.prompt: What does `i32.wrap_i64` do?

options.text: Truncates an `i64` to its lower 32 bits as an `i32`

questions.prompt: What does `f64.convert_i32_s` do?

options.text: Converts a signed 32-bit integer to a 64-bit IEEE-754 float

questions.prompt: What is the difference between `i32.reinterpret_f32` and `i32.trunc_f32_s`?

options.text: `reinterpret` copies the raw 32 IEEE-754 bits unchanged; `trunc` converts the numeric value toward zero

questions.prompt: What is `emscripten`'s `-sMODULARIZE=1` flag used for?

options.text: Wrapping generated JS glue in a factory function returning a Promise instead of polluting global `Module`

questions.prompt: Select all statements that are true about running Wasm inside a Web Worker.

options.text: Allows the worker to manipulate `document.getElementById` directly
Keeps heavy Wasm computation off the browser's main UI thread
Prevents UI freeze / poor INP during long calculations

questions.prompt: What does `i32.eqz` test on the top of the stack?

options.text: Whether the `i32` equals zero (pushes `1` if `0`, else `0`)

questions.prompt: Why does Wasm use `br_table` for large `switch` statements?

options.text: To perform O(1) indexed jump-table branching instead of a chain of `if/else` comparisons

questions.prompt: What does `wasm-tools validate app.wasm` verify?

options.text: That the `.wasm` binary conforms to WebAssembly specification validation rules

questions.prompt: Select all valid ways to reduce `.wasm` download size for web apps. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Strip debug info (`wasm-strip`) in release builds
Serve `.wasm` with Brotli or gzip compression
Embed uncompressed 4K textures inside Wasm `(data ...)` segments

questions.prompt: In Wasm, what is a `funcref`?

options.text: An opaque reference to a WebAssembly function stored in tables or passed as a value (Reference Types)

questions.prompt: What does `externref` allow in WebAssembly?

options.text: Passing opaque host objects (like DOM nodes or JS objects) through Wasm without copying them into linear memory

options.text: Strict CSPs block `WebAssembly.compile` unless `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` (or `'unsafe-eval'`) is permitted
